headline: Medium risk: shared-output and networked memory create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascade paths; no direct evidence of stronger isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a prompt-engineering content source, so its outputs can plausibly contain instruction-like text. Profile B has session memory and CLI/tooling, so if A’s content is fed into B, B may treat it as trusted context. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF A's content is copied into B's session memory or prompt context
IF B parses A-authored text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A-sourced text before passing it to B
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts
Review one sample A→B handoff for instruction-like strings
requires-engineering: add a parser that strips executable-looking directives

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while A is a content-writing repository with no data-class limits shown. If they share a workspace or if B uploads context through its API calls, sensitive material could leak into outputs or third-party inference. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem, clipboard, or prompt workspace
IF B sends context containing support or finance data to an external API
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Check B's outbound prompts for personal or finance data
Turn off any automatic file-to-prompt ingestion
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A shows no write or network capabilities, while B has allowlisted network egress and session-scoped memory. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is limited. The main risk is only if an external orchestrator gives A write access not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants A write access to the same mutable resource as B
IF B and A are both allowed to modify the same external state
mitigations: Keep A read-only
Do not mount shared writable directories
Verify B's allowlisted egress targets
requires-engineering: add resource locks for any shared mutable store

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated prompt-engineering source, so B may treat its content as authoritative examples or guidance. B’s session memory and API-backed workflow make it plausible that A’s text becomes operational input without a verification step. Because no direct handoff is documented, this is inferred, not proven.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as policy, facts, or workflow instructions
IF B acts on A's output without a human or rule-based verification step
mitigations: Require a verification step before B acts on A-derived content
Label A-derived content as non-authoritative
Spot-check one downstream workflow for unverified citations
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before execution

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while A has no compliance controls or residency guarantees shown. If A-derived content is mixed into B’s handling of regulated data, retention and residency obligations may diverge. Only B is cited because the compliance exposure is driven by B’s documented data classes; A lacks relevant controls to cite.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed through B while A-derived content is retained alongside it
IF retention or residency rules differ between A-hosted content and B-hosted data
mitigations: Classify B's regulated data flows
Confirm retention settings for B
Keep A content out of regulated B records
Document residency for any B API endpoints
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
